pathway.title: GENESIS ENERGY LP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The offshore pipeline franchise is the main support of the credit and its main concentration. It earned 67.74% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin on fee-based, life-of-lease dedications, and its revenue less operating costs has stayed between 71.05% and 74.87% of revenue since FY2023, so volume rather than cost sets its earnings. Throughput can grow without new spending: CHOPS ran at 66.39% of design capacity in the third quarter, and management says nine of the sixteen active deepwater rigs work leases dedicated to its facilities. Creditors hold a high-margin, low-capital cash stream whose size depends on producers' drilling. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F9

- Contract protection is real but short. Fixed and minimum-based offshore contract value still to be recognised equals 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue for 2027 and 13.91% for 2028, so earnings beyond 2028 rest mainly on producer volumes. The third quarter showed the floor at work: Shenandoah volumes fell below the minimum commitment and only the minimum was recognised, yet offshore Segment Margin still fell 3.50% in the quarter although it is 20.73% higher over the nine months. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation F10; calculation F7; calculation F6

- Expectations for 2026 earnings have eased at each of the three 2026 releases, which makes producer-sourced forecasting the weak point of the credit. The first-quarter release put Shenandoah at USD 12 million to USD 15 million less Segment Margin than original guidance and still aimed for the midpoint, the second said towards the lower end, and the third said near, or possibly below, the low end, with lower volumes from a couple of deepwater facilities expected into early 2027 until four new wells are completed. Management states that it relies heavily on operator information, so the recovery depends on well completions that Genesis does not control. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_a90ex9918kearnings_q12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation F33

- Leverage has improved on earnings, not repayment, and coverage stays thin. Total debt is 5.00x last-twelve-months EBITDA against 5.77x at the end of 2025 and 8.89x at the end of 2024, but carrying-value debt rose by USD 159.34 million in 2026. Net debt is 4.94x, and pro forma 4.98x after the common distribution payable on 2026-11-13 and 4.95x after the preferred distribution payable the same day, each taken separately. Cash interest cover is 2.41x and falls to 2.14x once distributions to minority holders are deducted from EBITDA, because the EBITDA used here includes their share. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F22; calculation F23; calculation F21; calculation F26

- Cash conversion has improved because growth spending ended, but working capital flatters the latest year. Operating cash flow less capital payments is USD 342,904 thousand over the last twelve months against USD 65,938 thousand in FY2025 and deficits in FY2024 and FY2023; excluding the working-capital inflow of USD 59,813 thousand it is USD 283,091 thousand. After net distributions to common, preferred and minority holders, USD 94,497 thousand remains before working capital, so debt reduction is possible but not yet demonstrated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 168–169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation F16; calculation F17; calculation F18; calculation F19

- Liquidity is adequate for about two years, and the real refinancing deadline is earlier than the note maturity. Revolver availability of USD 894.4 million is 1.49x the 2029 notes and liquidity is 3.52x last-twelve-months cash interest, and no note matures before 2029. But the credit agreement matures on 2028-10-16 if more than USD 150 million of the 2029 notes remain outstanding then, and the 2029 and 2030 maturities together are 36.91% of principal, so the notes must be addressed while leverage is above 5x. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–18; calculation F28; calculation F27; calculation F29

- Financial policy is the weakest dimension because cash is going to equity before debt. The partnership retired 41.15% of the preferred units for USD 221,594 thousand and raised the common distribution 21.21% above the level of a year ago while total debt rose, and it estimates that the 2026 financing steps cut its annual cost of capital by about USD 25 million. The saving is real, since the preferred coupon exceeds the cost of the new notes, but creditors carry more senior claims against the same earnings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F21; calculation F33

- Covenant terms tighten on a published timetable and compliance is not confirmed. The issuer's own bank ratio is 5.03x against a 5.75x maximum that falls to 5.50x after 2027, the minimum interest coverage rises from 2.00x to 2.15x in 2027 and 2.25x after that, and senior secured leverage is capped at 2.50x with the revolver undrawn. No 2026 filing states compliance, so these terms frame the downside rather than measure it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation F30

- Marine and onshore services diversify earnings but add little stability. Marine earned 17.38% and onshore 14.87% of nine-month Segment Margin; 77% of marine revenue was on term contracts in FY2025 and barge utilization is near full, while onshore keeps only 9.85% of revenue after product and operating costs and management ties its upside to market dislocations that could last into 2027. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation F13; calculation F14; calculation F12

runs.text: The strengths are the offshore franchise, the maturity and liquidity profile, and improved cash conversion; the weaknesses are concentration on producer-driven volumes, thin coverage at high leverage, shareholder-first financial policy, unreliable guidance and tightening covenant terms.

- Offshore franchise with low capital needs. Offshore pipelines earned 67.74% of nine-month Segment Margin on life-of-lease dedications and kept 72.79% of revenue after operating costs over the last twelve months; CHOPS used 66.39% of design capacity, so extra volume needs no new spending. That supports debt service as long as producers keep drilling. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation F1; calculation F5; calculation F9

- Maturity and liquidity profile. Nothing matures before 2029 and revolver availability of USD 894.4 million is 1.49x the 2029 notes, so debt service does not depend on market access for about two years. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–18; calculation F28

- Improved cash conversion. Growth capital spending fell 80.93% and operating cash flow less capital payments is USD 342,904 thousand over the last twelve months, which funds distributions and leaves USD 94,497 thousand before working capital. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; calculation F21; calculation F16; calculation F19

- Marine and onshore support. Barge utilization is near full and onshore pipeline volumes rose 35.49% in the third quarter, which cushions a weak offshore quarter but only modestly. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation F14

- Producer-driven concentration. Two-thirds of Segment Margin comes from offshore fields run by others, and the third-quarter Shenandoah shortfall cut offshore Segment Margin 3.50% even with a contract floor, so a longer shortfall flows to EBITDA and to coverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation F7

- Thin coverage at high leverage. Total debt is 5.00x EBITDA and cash interest cover is 2.41x, or 2.14x after minority distributions, so there is little earnings cushion before the 2027 covenant step-ups. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F22; calculation F26

- Shareholder-first financial policy. Preferred purchases and a 21.21% higher common distribution were made while total debt rose by USD 159.34 million, and the unseen debt documents may allow more of the same. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation F21

- Unreliable guidance. Expectations eased at each 2026 release and rest on operator information that Genesis does not control, so management's recovery timetable deserves a discount. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_a90ex9918kearnings_q12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Tightening covenant terms and a springing maturity. The leverage maximum falls to 5.50x after 2027, minimum coverage rises to 2.25x, and more than USD 150 million of the 2029 notes outstanding on 2028-10-16 matures the credit agreement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation F30; calculation F29

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-03-04 the partnership issued USD 750.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2034 and signed an Eighth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement that lifted revolver capacity from USD 800 million to USD 900 million and moved its maturity to 2031. Net proceeds of about USD 735.9 million bought USD 416.1 million of the 2028 notes in a tender that ended on 2026-03-20 and redeemed the remaining USD 263.3 million on 2026-03-22, with the rest helping to fund a preferred unit purchase on 2026-03-06. The partnership recorded a loss of USD 3.4 million on the tender premium, fees and written-off costs. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

On 2026-06-26 it signed a three-year USD 99.5 million receivables securitization facility priced at Term SOFR plus 1.375%, borrowed through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary whose receivables are not available to other creditors, and the facility is fully drawn. On 2026-06-03 it sold non-core natural gas pipeline and platform assets in the offshore segment for USD 95.0 million, recognising a gain of USD 17,436 thousand, and used the proceeds to buy preferred units on 2026-06-08. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Across 2026 the partnership bought preferred units on three dates for USD 221,594 thousand, which cut the class by 41.15%, and paid common distributions of USD 0.20 per unit for the second and third quarters. Its earlier 2025 transactions were the sale of the Alkali business for USD 1,425 million gross, the redemption of the 2027 notes, and a purchase of preferred units for USD 262.5 million. No new debt issue after 2026-09-30 is stated up to the cutoff, although whether a later event exists is not established because the quarterly report has no subsequent-events note. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B7

fields.value: This is the Business & governance fact pack for GENESIS ENERGY LP (issuer id gel), as of 2026-11-05. The pathway is the credit snapshot, run through Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit. The scope is the business, ownership, governance, capital-allocation and 2026 financing facts that matter to a creditor, drawn from the seven supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genesis Energy is a Gulf of America pipeline franchise with contracted but producer-dependent volumes, and in 2026 the partnership is directing improved cash flow to retiring preferred units and raising distributions while gross debt rises, which keeps noteholders reliant on continued offshore throughput.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Offshore pipelines produced 67.74% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin, and in the third quarter Shenandoah volumes fell below the minimum commitment, so only the minimum was recognised. Voting control rests with Class B units held mainly by one family, and the preferred investors keep a board observer right while they hold enough of the class. The executed debt documents that would bind these choices were not supplied, so the limits on distributions and further preferred purchases are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The offshore pipeline segment is the credit, and it is concentrated in a few producer-operated fields. It supplied 66.75% of FY2025 Segment Margin and 67.74% of the nine months of 2026, on contracts with minimum volume commitments and tiered fees, but its Segment Margin fell 3.50% in the third quarter because Shenandoah and legacy fields underperformed. The segment's results therefore track producer drilling, not the partnership's own spending, which is now complete.

fields.value: - Control is concentrated and creditors have no governance voice. Class B units elect the whole board, one family holds 76.9% of them and can appoint up to three directors, and the partnership has chosen not to follow listing rules on independent nominating and compensation committees. Creditors rely on contract terms, which are not supplied, rather than on governance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Preferred equity is shrinking quickly and its remaining holders keep influence. The partnership bought back 41.15% of the preferred units outstanding at the end of 2025 for USD 221,594 thousand in three purchases, at prices from the USD 33.71 issue price to USD 34.38. Two funds held 91.2% of the class at the end of 2025, and the filings do not say who sold. The remaining units carry an 11.24% coupon, and the initial purchasers keep a board observer right while they hold USD 200 million of the class.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is contractual and liquidity support: management says nine of sixteen active deepwater rigs work leases dedicated to flow through its facilities, four new high-impact wells are due to restore volumes, the revolver has USD 894.4 million available and no debt matures before 2029. The view would soften if offshore volumes returned above the minimum commitments for several quarters and the executed debt documents showed tight limits on distributions and preferred purchases. It would harden if volumes stayed weak into 2027, guidance for the year were missed, or distributions and preferred purchases continued to be funded with new debt.

fields.value: On 2026-03-04 the partnership issued USD 750.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2034 and signed an Eighth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement that lifted revolver capacity from USD 800 million to USD 900 million and moved its maturity to 2031. Net proceeds of about USD 735.9 million bought USD 416.1 million of the 2028 notes in a tender that ended on 2026-03-20 and redeemed the remaining USD 263.3 million on 2026-03-22, with the rest helping to fund a preferred unit purchase on 2026-03-06. The partnership recorded a loss of USD 3.4 million on the tender premium, fees and written-off costs.

fields.value: On 2026-06-26 it signed a three-year USD 99.5 million receivables securitization facility priced at Term SOFR plus 1.375%, borrowed through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary whose receivables are not available to other creditors, and the facility is fully drawn. On 2026-06-03 it sold non-core natural gas pipeline and platform assets in the offshore segment for USD 95.0 million, recognising a gain of USD 17,436 thousand, and used the proceeds to buy preferred units on 2026-06-08.

fields.value: Across 2026 the partnership bought preferred units on three dates for USD 221,594 thousand, which cut the class by 41.15%, and paid common distributions of USD 0.20 per unit for the second and third quarters. Its earlier 2025 transactions were the sale of the Alkali business for USD 1,425 million gross, the redemption of the 2027 notes, and a purchase of preferred units for USD 262.5 million. No new debt issue after 2026-09-30 is stated up to the cutoff, although whether a later event exists is not established because the quarterly report has no subsequent-events note.

fields.value: Genesis Energy is a Houston-based midstream partnership that earns fees in three businesses: offshore crude oil and natural gas pipelines in the Gulf of America, a U.S.-flag Jones Act marine fleet, and onshore crude pipelines with sulfur services on the Gulf Coast. Offshore fees are charged per barrel or under capacity arrangements that limit direct exposure to commodity prices, most production handled is under life-of-lease commitments, and 77% of marine revenue was on term contracts in FY2025. That gives the group visible cash flow while producers keep producing, but only about 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue is fixed or minimum-based for 2027, so visibility fades after 2028. Onshore revenue is largely crude marketing sales that carry thin margins. Debt service capacity is therefore supported by the offshore fee stream, liquidity is preserved by the end of growth spending, and refinancing confidence depends on offshore volumes holding while leverage is above 5x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Genesis Energy, L.P. is a listed partnership whose general partner it owns outright. Class B units elect the whole board, one family holds 76.9% of them and can appoint up to three directors, and holders of the preferred units keep a board observer right while they hold enough of the class. The partnership has chosen not to follow listing rules on independent nominating and compensation committees. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic guarantor subsidiaries, while the receivables facility sits in a bankruptcy-remote vehicle outside the guarantor group and its receivables are not available to other creditors. A financial party owns the remaining 36% of CHOPS and the consolidated Independence Hub also carries a noncontrolling interest, so part of consolidated EBITDA leaves the group as distributions to those holders. The credit implication is that control is concentrated, creditors have no governance voice, the 2026 pattern favours equity returns, and the structurally senior claims are the USD 99.5 million receivables facility and minority distributions equal to 11.32% of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Offshore revenue is volume-driven: fees are fixed per unit of volume under contracts or regulated tariffs, some contracts add capacity-reservation fees, and tiered fees step with cumulative throughput, so earnings follow producers' well performance and the number of rigs that can drill. The mechanism showed in the third quarter, when oil volumes were 0.99% lower and gas volumes 31.98% lower than a year earlier, Shenandoah fell below its minimum commitment and offshore Segment Margin fell 3.50%, although nine-month oil volumes were still 13.26% higher. For credit, offshore revenue is partly predictable through 2028, cyclical with drilling activity, concentrated by field, and exposed to hurricanes; pricing is set by contract and tariff, so growth comes from volume rather than price. Marine revenue is 77% term and 23% spot, utilization is near full and management reports robust spot rates, which supports renewals. Onshore pipeline volumes rose 35.49% in the third quarter, and the sulfur business holds 11 contracts with about two years remaining on average, so onshore is recurring in part but its upside is tied to dislocations. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in 2025, although Shell reached 11% in 2024, so customer concentration is moderate and the larger concentration is in producers behind a few fields.

fields.value: The offshore cost base is small relative to revenue and, on the evidence of a steady margin, largely fixed, so revenue less operating costs held between 71.05% and 74.87% of revenue from FY2023 to the last twelve months; that margin can be defended under volume pressure only until volumes fall below minimum commitments, after which each lost barrel falls almost entirely to EBITDA. Marine margin after operating costs slipped from 38.87% in FY2024 to 33.52% over the last twelve months; nine-month Segment Margin fell 3.70% on planned dry-docking days, although the third quarter rose 12.16%, and rebilled fuel and other costs that pass through enlarge revenue and costs together, so the percentage understates cash margin. The 23% spot share leaves marine open to rate swings. Onshore margin is 9.85% of revenue after product and operating costs and moves with crude marketing spreads and sulfur prices. Margins are therefore resilient to cost inflation but not to volume loss; the credit implication is that EBITDA is more sensitive to offshore throughput than to any cost lever.

Distributions to common, preferred and minority holders net of minority contributions took USD 188,594 thousand, leaving USD 94,497 thousand before working capital, and the preferred redemptions of USD 221,594 thousand were funded in part by new borrowing. Capex flexibility is good because growth spending is complete and distributions are discretionary, so EBITDA converts to cash that can service debt, but only a small part has been used to reduce debt so far.

fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate. Offshore pipelines compete on proximity, cost of connection, capacity, rates and onshore access, and producers could build their own handling facilities; marine carriers compete with other pipelines, rail and trucking. Dedicated leases reduce the risk for offshore, so rivalry matters most for marine and onshore margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is low: the annual report cites high capital costs, tariff regulation and the cost of acquiring rights-of-way as barriers for pipelines, management calls its deepwater system irreplaceable, and the Jones Act restricts domestic marine capacity to U.S.-built, U.S.-owned vessels; this supports the stability of fees rather than their growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is limited for offshore crude, which must reach shore by pipe, and moderate for marine, where pipeline, rail and trucking compete for the same barrels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is moderate: customers are large producers and refiners, none above 10% of revenue in 2025, but term contracts and life-of-lease commitments limit switching, while marine spot business is more exposed to buyers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is high in a specific sense: producers supply the volumes and drilling rigs supply the pace, and management names rig availability as the constraint, so the suppliers of volume hold the key lever over Genesis' cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and weather are material and the rest of the political, economic, social and technological headings are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence. Federal regulation of tariffs and of pipeline integrity applies to the pipelines, the Jones Act protects marine competition, and management points to the Iranian situation and renewed imports from Venezuela as drivers of onshore dislocations that may fade, while the earnings release lists tariffs and military conflicts among its risks. Weather is a direct operating risk: early-October hurricane disruption cost about four days of offshore service, and the annual report notes that virtually all operations are exposed to storms. Commodity prices matter to the credit through producer drilling decisions rather than through direct exposure, because offshore fees limit direct exposure to price. Most debt is fixed rate; the floating-rate exposure is the receivables facility and any revolver borrowing, which is small at present.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: an irreplaceable offshore pipeline franchise with life-of-lease dedications, a low capital need now that growth projects are done, no maturity before 2029, and USD 894.4 million of undrawn revolver. Weaknesses: 5.00x leverage and 2.41x cash interest cover, concentration in producer-run fields, a shareholder-first financial policy and concentrated control. Opportunities: four new wells and the Monument tieback could lift offshore volumes without new spending by Genesis, onshore dislocations may last into 2027, and management targets further annual savings of USD 50 million to USD 60 million from right-sizing the capital structure. Threats: hurricane disruption, drilling delays or disappointing wells, a covenant timetable that tightens in 2027 and after, and the October 2028 test on the 2029 notes.

fields.value: The trend is improving on leverage, from 8.89x to 5.00x, and on cash conversion, while coverage and financial policy limit the gain; the missing data are the executed debt documents, covenant calculations and field-level contract terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the offshore recovery is the swing factor. Two Monument wells are due by the end of the first quarter of 2027 or in the first half, a fifth Shenandoah well by the end of 2027, and two rigs are drilling wells for the Salamanca facility; this supports volumes and offshore margin if completed on time, and leaves the fourth quarter of 2026 near or below the low end of guidance. Marine has near-full utilization, robust spot rates and no major dry-docking until 2027, a tailwind for term renewals; onshore benefits from dislocations that management says could last into 2027. Headwinds are producer underperformance, hurricane season, the covenant step-ups from 2027 and the 2029 note test in October 2028. Over three to five years the franchise benefits from two new rigs expected to enter service and from known discoveries awaiting development, but contract floors decline each year after 2027, so earnings rest more on producer volumes. For credit, the next year decides whether leverage falls on earnings alone or whether debt must be repaid to keep the covenant cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with producer underperformance that outlasts management's timetable: Shenandoah stays at its minimum commitment, legacy fields remain curtailed, the Monument wells slip beyond the first half of 2027, and a weak hurricane season adds shut-ins. The first operational break is offshore volume, because offshore margin falls almost one for one once volumes are below the contract floors, and the floors cover only 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue in 2027. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA with fixed interest: a fall of 12.98% in last-twelve-months EBITDA would put statement-derived leverage at 5.75x and a fall of 16.94% would put cash interest cover at 2.00x, which are reference points at the covenant levels on statement-based measures, not a covenant test, and the 2.15x and 2.25x levels are reached at falls of 10.71% and 6.56%. A fall of 16.94% equals 24.84% of offshore revenue less operating costs, so the scenario requires roughly a quarter of the offshore margin to disappear. The liquidity, leverage and refinancing consequence is that availability under the revolver would depend on covenant compliance and the October 2028 test, so the partnership would need to cut distributions, hold back preferred purchases and refinance the 2029 notes early. Management levers are real: growth capital spending is finished, distributions are discretionary, and USD 894.4 million of revolver availability can bridge a few quarters. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis before 2029, but not sufficient to keep leverage falling if volumes stay at the third-quarter level through 2027. The observable triggers are Shenandoah staying at its minimum commitment after the Monument wells connect, guidance missed at the low end, and revolver borrowing used to pay distributions. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage while the covenant levels tighten.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Genesis Energy presents an adequate business profile supported by an irreplaceable offshore pipeline franchise with low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by 5.00x leverage, 2.41x cash interest cover, producer-dependent volumes and a shareholder-first financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because offshore margins are stable and growth spending is finished, though working capital flattered the latest year. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on offshore volumes recovering in 2027, the covenant timetable and early action on the 2029 notes before the October 2028 test. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage as covenant levels tighten. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant compliance calculations, field-level contract terms and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis complete. Top risk: offshore volumes staying below expectations through 2027 while leverage stays above 5x.
